title: As US ties fray, Canada turns to Turkey for defense, nuclear cooperation
gist: Canadian PM Mark Carney made the first bilateral visit by a Canadian prime minister to Turkey, launching a strategic partnership with defense, energy, nuclear and trade goals as US-Canada frictions open space for Ankara.

insights.claim: Frictions between Washington and Ottawa are opening a strategic window for Turkey to deepen defense-tech, nuclear and investment ties with Canada under a new strategic partnership.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: Middle powers are hedging away from US dependence; watch Turkish defense exports and Canadian procurement diversification.

insights.claim: Mark Carney on Oct. 22 became the first Canadian prime minister to make a bilateral visit to Turkey, accompanied by Energy Minister Tim Hodgson and Foreign Minister Anita Anand.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: Delegation composition signals energy and security priorities.

insights.claim: Canada and Turkey aim to raise bilateral trade from $3 billion to $5 billion within five years, targeting eventually $10 billion.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: Modest base but a stated tripling target; track follow-through in sectors like defense, energy and mining.

insights.claim: The two countries signed three MOUs on defense industry cooperation, aviation and energy, and agreed to hold the first round of free trade agreement talks in Ankara in November.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: A concrete FTA timeline creates near-term catalyst for Turkish defense and aviation exporters' access to Canada.

insights.claim: Erdogan and Carney announced a three-year plan to increase trade, mutual investment and cooperation in defense, energy and mining, though no further details were provided.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: Details are thin; treat as signaling until specifics emerge.
